### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2420778c763cf5eaa92cf559582ecdf70d6274e5`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **20** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2420778c763cf5eaa92cf559582ecdf70d6274e5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `db902bf44e893755da8a875c5748fcd7be2b820e` — the merge of head `b55451a4568c13e077880b6a1dec7281f0b2a684` into base `2420778c763cf5eaa92cf559582ecdf70d6274e5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin db902bf44e893755da8a875c5748fcd7be2b820e && git checkout db902bf44e893755da8a875c5748fcd7be2b820e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2420778c763cf5eaa92cf559582ecdf70d6274e5 b55451a4568c13e077880b6a1dec7281f0b2a684 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2420778c763cf5eaa92cf559582ecdf70d6274e5 && git merge --no-ff b55451a4568c13e077880b6a1dec7281f0b2a684

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2420778c763cf5eaa92cf559582ecdf70d6274e5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2420778c763cf5eaa92cf559582ecdf70d6274e5` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `b38c236021b01ebd317aa863b9e089b1d4776b43`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #29408 (body and all 5 comments: triage 6580439865, claims 6581219297 / 6581272888, dev report 6584231973), PR #29528 (body, 9-file list, net diff against `main` 5651647d8), the check-runs on the head. Cited code on `main` was read to judge the diff (`declared-read-columns.ts`, `engine.ts` find / findOne / `applyFormulaPlan` / `withoutFormulaWidening`, `engine-secret-internal-fields.ts`, plugin-security `field-masker.ts`, spec `injected-system-column-provenance.ts` and `resolveInjectedSystemColumns`).

### ① Derived judgments

The diff changes no accept set: nothing a request may send is refused or newly admitted, and no request validation, projection check, error code or published type moves. The changes are all on the record body a read answers:

1. **A selected stored declared column that the driver did not return is now answered `null` on `find` / `findOne`. RIGHT.** It is the card's "Wanted" exactly. The fill runs once per verb, right after the #21571 shaping, on `driverAst.fields`. So a `beforeFind` rewrite counts. Every door on the two verbs inherits it: `getData`, `findData` / list, `expand` sub-reads (via `this.find`), export and search. `withSelectedColumnsAnswered` copies the row and never mutates it. On driver-sql this is a no-op for every local declared non-formula column (`fieldHasColumn` gives each one a column).
2. **A column the projection does not name stays absent. RIGHT.** Only string entries the stored set holds are selected. Widening is not selecting: the formula-input and file-owner `id` keys are filled, then cut by `rowsWithoutFormulaWidening` / `withoutFormulaWidening`, which delete by key whatever the value is. Read on `main`, and pinned by the `doubled` case.
3. **A column field-level security refuses stays absent. RIGHT.** `FieldMasker.maskRecord` runs in the security middleware's post-phase, after the verb body, and `delete`s every hidden field unconditionally. A partial-mask rule maps `null` to `null` (`maskFieldValue`), and so does `maskSecretFields` (`row[field] == null ? null : SECRET_MASK`). `omitInternalFields` deletes. Pinned on SQLite with `SecurityPlugin` composed (6 tests), and ablation A3 (fill moved after the mask) reds 2 of them.
4. **A formula field is not filled. RIGHT. But its VALUE changes on mongo / memory, and the PR does not declare that. Should-fix S1.** `applyFormulaPlan` evaluates CEL against the raw row (`record: scope`), not a materialized one. At base, on a sparse driver, a formula that reads an unwritten declared field faults on the missing key and answers `null`, with a fault reported to the sink. On head it evaluates against `null`. The PR's own pin shows this: `doubled = record.qty != null ? record.qty * 2 : -1` reads `-1`. At base it would read `null` plus a fault. The new behavior is the right one: it is SQL's answer and the `materializeDeclaredFields` IN-HAND rule. But the PR body and changeset claim "every read returns the same rows and the same values" and that a formula "keeps its computed value". That is not true on mongo / memory for any formula over an unwritten field, and `has(record.x)` inside a formula flips from false to true there too.
5. **An injected column that a federated object does not provision stays absent. RIGHT, as far as `unprovisionedInjectedColumns` reaches. A residual gap: should-fix S2.** `PLATFORM_PROVISIONED_COLUMNS` (`id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`) joins every `declaredColumnSet` unconditionally. `unprovisionedInjectedColumns` lists only columns the registry injected. On an `external` object with `systemFields: false` or `systemFields: { audit: false }`, nothing is injected (spec pin: `unprovisionedInjectedColumns({ ...external(), systemFields: false })` is `[]`). So `created_at` / `updated_at` stay in the stored set, and a remote table without them is now answered `created_at: null, updated_at: null`. That happens on driver-sql too, where base answered no key. It is the very case the PR's own rule ("no storage behind it, so there is no persisted state to answer for") excludes, and it contradicts the declaration's "SQL unchanged". The value is only `null` and the reach is narrow (federated objects that opt out of system fields), so it is not a must-fix.
6. **A name outside the declared set is never added. RIGHT.** The intersection runs with `declaredColumnSet`, so this cannot widen what #21571 serves. Pinned, and ablation A2 reds it.
7. **In-process readers now see the total record on mongo / memory. RIGHT, and named in the changeset.** These are `afterFind` hooks, `expand` targets, file-reference resolution, and flow `get_record` → later nodes. A hook or client that told absent from `null` (`'x' in row`, `has(record.x)`) now reads what SQL already answered. A GET → PUT round-trip client now sends explicit `null`s and stores them where the key was absent. That is parity with SQL, and the accept set is unchanged.
8. **Not covered, rightly out of scope: `count`, `aggregate` (including its `driver.find` bucketing fallback) and `distinct`.** They answer no record bodies. `readUpdatePriorRow`, the pre-image reads and the write echoes are unchanged, as the PR names.
9. **The write echo now diverges from the read on mongo / memory.** An insert or update answers sparse, and the next GET answers total. On SQL both are total. `hydrateWriteFormulas`' read-your-write rule ("the write response is now the same materialization a read produces") is the precedent this leaves open. This is open_question 2, answered in ③.
10. **The PR breaks an in-process reader that tells absent from `null`, and CI shows it. WRONG: must-fix M1.** `Test Core (6/8)` fails `@objectstack/plugin-audit` `src/objects/sys-audit-log-record-views-columns.test.ts`, case "ip_address specifically stays out — the read writer structurally cannot stamp it". The assertion at line 206 is `expect(stampedKeys.has('ip_address')).toBe(false)`, which received `true`. That test derives "the keys the read writer stamped" by reading the persisted `sys_audit_log` row back through `engine.find` on a sparse stub driver. On head, that read now answers every declared `sys_audit_log` column, `ip_address` included, as `null`, so the key set is the declared set and not the stamped set. Its sibling `it.each` ("column %s is a key the read writer actually stamps") still passes, but it has become vacuous: it now passes for ANY declared column, so the #9539 guard no longer guards. This is caused by this diff, not inherited: the failing read is exactly the fill in ①1, and the dev's suite list (objectql, rest, runtime, driver-mongodb, driver-memory) does not include plugin-audit.
11. **Forced test edits in the diff. RIGHT.** The five Expand cases and the formula-trim CONTROL each move because a test-double row lacks a declared column (`created_at` / `updated_at` / registry-injected `queue`) that a whole read now answers. None of them relaxes an assertion. The `federated-injected-column-readers` census row (`excludes`) is the right disposition for the new seam.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/objectql: patch`. RIGHT. A bug fix in a released package, non-protocol, with nothing BREAKING. The other two packages the diff touches (runtime, driver-mongodb) gain test files only and publish nothing.
- `Clause-②: no`. RIGHT. No accept set moves (①). The response gains `null` keys, which is not a widening or a narrowing of what a request may send.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`. RIGHT. Nothing a metadata author can write changes.
- The changeset prose is WRONG on two sentences: "every read returns the same rows and the same values" (see ①4 and ①5), and "Who sees it", which omits formula values on mongo / memory. That is S1 and S2. The level is unaffected.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Real mongod NOT MEASURED (fake `Db`).** Accepted. The fill is driver-agnostic and runs in the engine after the driver answers. Real mongod only bears on the base premise (no key for an unwritten field), and the card already cites it from `mongodb-driver.ts`. The fake `Db` projects as mongod does: named keys the document has. Not escalated.
- **open_question 1 (driver-memory real-driver pin).** Answer: **A**. A new consumer under `check:driver-memory-census` is a maintainer ruling (#6664) that this card does not hold. The seam is driver-agnostic, and the objectql sparse driver reproduces the memory shape. No escalation is needed for this card.
- **open_question 2 (write echoes sparse on mongo / memory).** Answer: **B**. The seat files a follow-up. The card's business reason (one record, two shapes) survives on the create / update response a client renders first. ①9 is now a read-vs-echo divergence on the same driver, against the `hydrateWriteFormulas` read-your-write precedent. Escalated to the seat to file.
- **Dogfood: 4 local failures claimed pre-existing.** These are `flow-runas` ×3 and `declarative-endpoint-anonymous-guest` ×1. The dev's control (fill disabled at both call sites, objectql rebuilt) fails the same 4 of 12, which is a sound base-equivalence control. CI did not run the battery on this head: `Dogfood Regression Gate` = success, "satisfied — no shard was expected to run" (the filter skipped all 3 shards and `Dogfood Verify CLI`). So the gate's verdict is a filter skip, not a pass on this change. The dev's `out_of_scope_findings` entry goes to the seat to dedupe and file. Dogfood ran on `7daf9652`, and the only later commit is a driver-mongodb test file outside the dogfood closure. Accepted.
- **Other deviations** (the A3 rerun, the gate rerun on the final head, the PR opened without assignees): process only, accepted.
- **PR author** is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so there is no separate author note.
- **Check-runs on the head** (read at 18:09Z, after waiting about 14 minutes): 33 success, 13 skipped, 1 failure, and the `Test Core` aggregate is still queued. The one failure is `Test Core (6/8)`, the plugin-audit case in ①10 (M1). Every Lint / Type Check / Build / guard run is green.

**Must-fix:**
- **M1.** `Test Core (6/8)` is red, caused by this change (①10). Re-derive `stampedKeys` in `sys-audit-log-record-views-columns.test.ts` from the stub driver's stored row, not from an engine read. That keeps both the `ip_address` pin and the per-column `it.each` meaningful again, rather than relaxing either one. Then run every package whose tests read records back through `find` / `findOne` on a sparse double, not only the four suites listed, and report them. Any other such pin is the same class of failure.

**Should-fix:**
- **S1.** Correct the PR body and changeset declaration lines ("the same values" and the formula sentence). Add to "Who sees it": a formula reading an unwritten field now evaluates against `null` on mongo / memory (it used to answer `null` with a fault), as it already did on SQL. Pin the base → head value move if the follow-up touches it.
- **S2.** On an `external` object, a `PLATFORM_PROVISIONED_COLUMNS` timestamp that the registry did not inject (`systemFields: false` or `audit: false`) should be left out of `selectedStoredColumns`, with a pin. This lands here or as a follow-up card.
- **Follow-up (open_question 2 → B):** a card for the write echo on mongo / memory.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `b55451a4568c13e077880b6a1dec7281f0b2a684`
Local-runs: none

Round 2. Round 1 (issuecomment-6584622486, head `b38c2360`) was FAIL with M1, S1 and S2. This record judges the whole PR on the new head, not only the deltas.

Inputs read: card #29408 (body and all 5 comments: triage 6580439865, claims 6581219297 / 6581272888, dev reports 6584231973 and 6589029634), PR #29528 (body, 10-file list, net diff against `main`), the round-1 record, and the 52 check-runs on the head. Cited code on `main` was read to judge the diff: `declared-read-columns.ts`, `federated-object.ts` (`isFederatedObject`), spec `injected-system-column-provenance.ts` (`platformProvisionsStorage`, `unprovisionedInjectedColumns`), driver-sql table creation and `stampInsertTimestamps`, and the insert-time timestamp stamping in driver-memory and driver-mongodb.

### ① Derived judgments

The diff still changes no accept set. Nothing a request may send is refused or newly admitted, and no validation, projection check, error code or published type moves. Every change is to the record body a read answers. Round-1 judgments ①1 to ①9 and ①11 hold on this head: `engine.ts` has the same two call sites on `driverAst.fields`, and the fill, the projection and widening rule, the FLS ordering and the declared-set intersection are unchanged. The round-2 changes:

1. **M1 is closed. The #9539 guard guards again. RIGHT.** `sys-audit-log-record-views-columns.test.ts` now builds `stampedKeys` from `driver.storedRows('sys_audit_log')`. That is a copy of the stub's stored map, so it holds exactly what `driver.create` received, before any read shapes it. The engine read stays only as a one-row count check. Both assertions are still strict: the `it.each` still checks `stampedKeys.has(column)` with `toBe(true)` over every `record_views` column, and `ip_address` is still checked with `toBe(false)`, next to `not.toContain('ip_address')` on the view. On base, the read-back went through `withDeclaredColumnsOnly` on a stub that returns the row as stored. So the stored key set is the old observed set plus any undeclared key the writer passed, and every view column is a declared field. No assertion became weaker. The dev's ablation A5 (the writer stamps `ip_address`) turns the named case red. On CI, `Test Core (6/8)`, the shard that failed in round 1, is green. The sweep that round 1 asked for was run: 23 more packages that boot a real `ObjectQL` all exit 0, and only plugin-audit needed a change. `Test Core` 8/8 agrees.
2. **S2 is closed. `selectedStoredColumns` no longer fills a federated object's undeclared platform timestamp. RIGHT.** The new skip is `federated && name !== 'id' && !hasOwn(fields, name)`. The only names in `declaredColumnSet` that are not field-map keys are `PLATFORM_PROVISIONED_COLUMNS`, so the skip can only drop `created_at` / `updated_at` on an `external` object whose field map does not hold them. `isFederatedObject` is `external != null`, which is the negation of the spec's `platformProvisionsStorage`, so it draws the same line as `unprovisionedInjectedColumns`. I checked each question:
   - **`id` is still answered.** It is exempt by name, and the pin's three read shapes assert `row.id`.
   - **A declared remote timestamp is still answered `null`.** A declared `updated_at` is a field-map key, so it is kept. The `REMOTE_MAPPED` case pins `updated_at: null` with `created_at` absent.
   - **The default federated case is unchanged.** There the registry injects the timestamps, they are field-map keys, and they are `injected-unprovisioned`, so `unprovisionedInjectedColumns` still excludes them. The `FEDERATED stays absent` case pins it.
   - **The rule takes away no value a driver returned.** It only shrinks the set that gets `null`-filled. `withDeclaredColumnsOnly` still serves any `created_at` a remote returns, for example one mapped through `external.columnMap`.
   - **A non-federated object with `systemFields: false` or `audit: false` is not affected, and keeping its three columns is right.** driver-sql creates `created_at` / `updated_at` on every table it builds (`createAuditTimestampColumn`, unconditional) and stamps them. driver-memory (`memory-driver.ts` create and bulk paths) and driver-mongodb (`mongodb-driver.ts` create, `bulkCreate` and the upsert `$setOnInsert`) stamp both on every insert, whatever `systemFields` says. So a local opted-out object has a stored timestamp on all three drivers. Only a row written outside those doors could read `null`, and there `null` is the honest answer for a provisioned column. It is pinned by `a local object keeps the provisioned three whatever systemFields says`.
   - **Coverage.** The pins cover `systemFields: false` and `systemFields.audit: false`, on whole, list and naming reads. The dev's ablation A6 (exclusion removed) turns 3 cases red. The census gains `selectedStoredColumns :: isFederatedObject()` with `excludes`, the right disposition.
3. **S1 is closed. The declaration now tells the formula change. RIGHT.** The changeset's `Clause-②` line no longer says "the same values". It says "every value a driver returned is answered as before", which is true: a formula's value is the engine's, not the driver's. It also states that a `formula` over an unwritten column on mongo / memory now evaluates against `null`, as on SQL. "Who sees it" gives the before and after (`null` before, `-1` now), and the dev measured the old value with the fill disabled. The PR body matches.
4. **The main merge brought in nothing new. RIGHT.** `a3cdd97a` merges `390bd2ae`. Comparing `390bd2ae...a3cdd97a` gives exactly the PR's 10 files with the PR's own hunks, so the merge resolution added nothing. Main's commits that the merge brought in touch nothing in `engine.ts`, `declared-read-columns.ts`, the census test or plugin-audit. `b55451a4` changes one test fixture's typing (an inline literal becomes a variable) and nothing else. Main has since moved 46 commits past `390bd2ae`, including `engine.ts`, `registry.ts` and the census file. GitHub reports the PR as `unstable`, not `dirty`, so there is no textual conflict. The one new `find` consumer there, `serveReferenceNames`, tests `== null`, so it does not tell absent from `null`. This is for information only: the merge path re-tests it, and it is not a finding on this head.
5. **No new must-fix or should-fix was found on this head.**

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/objectql: patch`. RIGHT. It is a bug fix in a released, non-protocol package, and nothing is BREAKING. runtime, driver-mongodb and plugin-audit gain or change test files only and publish nothing. `Check Changeset` is green.
- `Clause-②: no`. RIGHT. No accept set moves (①). The line now names the response's `null` keys and the formula value move without claiming that values are unchanged.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`. RIGHT.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Round-1 rulings stand.** open_question 1 is A (no driver-memory census consumer). open_question 2 is B: the seat filed follow-up #29538 for the write echoes. The round-2 report has `open_questions: []`, and nothing is newly open.
- **Real mongod NOT MEASURED, still the driver's fake `Db`.** Accepted, as in round 1. The fill is engine-side and driver-agnostic.
- **Round-2 deviations.** These are the 2h background limit (example-crm and dogfood were re-run and passed) and the ablation-replace restore of an uncommitted edit (the fix was re-applied, committed and re-ablated). Both are process only and accepted.
- **Dogfood.** On CI, `Dogfood Regression Gate` is success, but its 3 shards and `Dogfood Verify CLI` are skipped by the filter, so CI did not run the battery. The dev ran it locally on `a3cdd97a` under the lock: 3277 passed, 0 failed. The only later commit is an objectql test-file type fix, which is outside the dogfood closure. The round-1 `flow-runas` / anonymous-guest reds are gone after #29451. Accepted.
- **Check-runs on the head.** I read them at 2026-11-02T21:38Z and again at 2026-11-02T21:41Z: 52 runs, all completed, 37 success, 15 skipped, 0 failure. `Test Core` 1/8 to 8/8 and the aggregate are green. Every Type Check run is green, including `Type Check · workspace`, which was red on `a3cdd97a`. Every Lint, Build and guard run is green, as are `Check PR Size` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. The skips are UI, opt-in and dogfood-filter jobs this diff does not reach.
